key_insight: The paper turns failed LLM-agent rollouts into a large, reusable error-to-diagnosis dataset and shows that evidence-checked corrections can substantially improve failure recovery.
engineering_relevance: For agentic systems, the dataset and training pipeline offer a practical way to diagnose recurring errors and fine-tune policies using recorded traces instead of rerunning expensive environment rollouts.
method: Built the Agent Error Dataset (AED) with 50,228 error-diagnosis pairs from 9,961 tasks spanning 33 environments, 19 harness families, and 23 policy models.
Designed a five-stage Agentic Error-to-Training (AET) pipeline to collect failures, generate diagnoses and corrections, and verify them against stored execution evidence.
Separated training views for diagnosis and actor recovery, and compared corrections with replayed retries when matched replay support was available.
evidence_signal: Across 3,062 matched replay pairs, first-proposal corrections increased verifier pass rates from 18.4% to 51.1%, and diagnosis fine-tuning raised exact-step agreement from 47.2% to 63.6% on a 943-case holdout.
watch_item: Results depend on recorded traces, execution metadata, and replay support, so portability may be limited in environments without consistent logging or reproducible checkpoints.
paper_title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training
